names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 13 mai, «Sfântul Cuvios Gheorghe Ivirul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Γεώργιος ο Ίβηρας», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 13 May, „Преподобни Јован, Јевтимије Георгије и Гаврил Иверски.“ — Преподобни left off, which is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types`, and **Иверски kept**, the epithet "the Iberian" the heading sets after all four names and which the entry's first sentence confirms belongs to all four. Measured: a bare «Георгије» would fold with `george-of-mytilene`, where this form folds with nothing. The heading prints no comma between Јевтимије and Георгије; that is the book's and is quoted as it stands rather than corrected. The translation of the Scriptures and the 1066 are in the body.

birth.note: The first birth year any book has given him; the folder held none. The Охридски пролог for 30. јун ст. ст. opens his entry „Рођен у Иверији или Грузији 1014. године као сродник царева грузијских.“ — born in Iveria or Georgia in 1014, a kinsman of the Georgian kings. The country is given as two names for one place and not as a choice, and the kinship is to kings the entry does not name (6 October 2026).

death.note: Two books and three statements, and this is the widening rather than a choice. doxologia’s page title gave the flat 1066 this folder held, its body no year; the Охридски пролог for 13. мај ст. ст. said 1066 as well. The same Пролог for 30. јун ст. ст.: „У старости пожели да сконча у Светој Гори, куда се и крене, но смрт га стигне у Цариграду 1067. године.“ — in his old age he wished to end his days on the Holy Mountain and set out for it, but death caught him at Constantinople in 1067. One book against itself on two of its own days, so the interval is opened to hold both and neither year is preferred (6 October 2026).

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).

feast.note: doxologia.ro's calendar keeps him on 13 mai with the other Iberian founders, and its own page for him ends «Deși a adormit pe 24 Mai, georgienii prăznuiesc pomenirea lui pe 30 iunie, rânduindu-l împreună cu Sfinții Apostoli. Se cinstește pe 13 Mai.» — so the page itself names three days and settles on this one.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on — and the Romanian row already carries a note that doxologia.ro's own page for him names three days and settles on this one. saint.gr adds no fourth day. **He is none of the corpus's many other Georges**, which the namesweep flagged and which were read; the office settles it. **The Greek entry is one sentence long** and it is the one thing the corpus wanted: «εξελέγη ηγούμενος της μονής των Ιβήρων του Αγίου Όρους μετά την παραίτηση του Οσίου Ευθυμίου και κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη» — elected abbot of Iviron after the resignation of the venerable Euthymius, and asleep in peace. **Note the word «παραίτηση», resignation**: Euthymius's own page on the same day says he died at Constantinople in 1028 and says nothing of resigning, and saint.gr is not reconciled here — the difference is recorded and nothing is inferred from it. **No year at all**, so the existing `dates` object is not touched and nothing is added to it. **Euthymius is linked.** No hymn is printed.

feast.note: **A SECOND PROLOGUE DAY, WRITTEN AS A §4 SECOND-DAY NOTE AND NOT AS A ROW, AND THE ENTRY EXPLAINS BOTH DAYS ITSELF.** The same book gives him a whole entry of his own on the Julian 30 June, headed „Преподобни Георгије Иверски.“, and closes it „Иако је умро 24. маја, Иверци празнују спомен његов 30. јуна сматрајући га равноапостолним.“ — although he died on 24 May, the Iverians keep his memory on 30 June, reckoning him equal to the apostles. The note above already recorded, off the Romanian page, that 30 June is the day the Georgians keep him with the Apostles; **this is that statement arriving from a fourth book with a full life attached to it, and it is the first of the three days this book has been seen to print an entry under besides the 13 May this row keeps**. An attestation holds one feast, so 13 May stays and he does not render on 30 June here; the row above is **copied back out of this folder unchanged** by the day’s generator, which asserts it venerated on 13/5 before it appends, and only this note is added. **A BIRTH YEAR THE FOLDER NEVER HAD AND A DEATH YEAR THAT DISAGREES WITH THE ONE IT HELD.** „Рођен у Иверији или Грузији 1014. године као сродник царева грузијских.“ — born in Iveria or Georgia in 1014, a kinsman of the Georgian kings — is the first birth year any of the four books has given him, and it is written. And „У старости пожели да сконча у Светој Гори, куда се и крене, но смрт га стигне у Цариграду 1067. године.“ puts his death at Constantinople in **1067**, where this folder carried a flat 1066 off the title of doxologia’s page and the Prologue’s own 13 May entry said 1066 too. **The same book gives two different years on two of its own days.** The death is widened to 1066—1067 rather than moved, which is what `polycarp-of-alexandria` and `theodosia-of-tyre` are on file for; nothing is chosen between them and the disagreement is in the `dates` note and in the life. **равноапостолним IS REFUSED AND IT IS THE CLEANEST CASE OF THAT REFUSAL YET.** The closing sentence has the Iverians reckon him equal to the apostles, `equal-to-the-apostles` is in §5’s table, and it is still not written: it is in the body and not in the heading, which gives only Преподобни, and it is in any case reported of the Iverians rather than asserted. `types` untouched at `venerable`, `monk` and `abbot`. **AUTHOR: you may write it.** **WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS AND WHAT IS REFUSED FROM IT.** „Помоћу цара Константина Мономаха обновио Ивер и покрио цркву оловом.“ and „Тај оловни кров и до данас стоји.“ — with the help of the emperor Constantine Monomachos he renewed Iviron and roofed the church with lead, and that lead roof stands to this day; „Превео на грузински језик Свето Писмо, Пролог и богослужбене књиге.“ adds the Prologue itself and the service books to the Scriptures the 13 May entry had him translate; „Цар Баграт позове га у Грузију, да учи народ.“ has the emperor Bagrat call him to Georgia to teach the people, where the 13 May reading had an empress of Georgia employ him on missions. Neither emperor holds a folder and neither takes a row; the spiritual father of „Подвизавао се код чувеног духовника Георгија у гори Црној.“, the famous elder George on the Black Mountain, holds none either and Ruling 3 refuses him. No `locations`: Iveria, the Black Mountain, the Holy Mountain, Georgia and Constantinople are all named in clauses. No name form: this folder already stores Георгије Иверски in `sr` off the 13 May heading, and this heading gives the same two words under a different rank. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person. **THE DAY’S FIRST ENTRY PRODUCES NOTHING, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST §5 CASE OF THE WAVE.** „Сабор светих славних и свехвалних апостола.“ is the Synaxis of the holy, glorious and all-praised Apostles: „Мада сваки од дванаест великих апостола има свој нарочити дан празновања у години, ипак је црква одредила овај дан као саборни празник свих укупно, и уз њих Павла.“ — though each of the twelve great apostles has his own particular day of celebration in the year, the Church appointed this day as the common feast of all of them together, and Paul with them. **The heading enumerates nobody**, so by §5 it is one entry and no row, and a person narrated in a body but not named in a heading gets none either. **The body enumerates all thirteen completely**, with each man’s own days: „Ово су имена и ово су дани посебног празновања свете Дванаесторице: Петар – 29. јуна и 16. јануара; Андреј – 30. новембра; Јаков Зеведејев – 30. априла; Јован Богослов – 26. септембра и 8. маја; Филип -14. новембра; Вартоломеј – 11. јуна и 25. августа; Тома – 6. октобра; Матеј Јеванђелист – 16. новембра; Јаков Алфејев – 9. октобра; Тадеј (или Јуда Јаковљев) – 19. јуна; Симон Зилот – 10. маја; Матија – 9. августа; Павле – 29. јуна;“ And then it enumerates their deaths: „Да поменемо још овде, како је који од ових најсветијих и најкориснијих људи у историји света скончао свој земни живот: Петар – распет наопако; Андреј – распет; Јаков Зеведејев – посечен; Јован Богослов – упокојио се чудесно; Филип – распет; Вартоломеј – распет, па одеран и посечен; Тома – избоден са пет копља; Матеј – огњем сажежен; Јаков Алфејев – распет; Тадеј – распет; Симон Зилот – распет; Матеј – каменован, па мртав посечен секиром; Павле – посечен.“ Every one of the thirteen is a folder this corpus already keeps, and **not one row, name form, date or type is written from this entry**.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.05.2026 (13. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Јован, Јевтимије Георгије и Гаврил Иверски.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, an enumerated company of four, so one row each. **THE 1066 AGREES EXACTLY AND NOTHING IN `dates` WAS TOUCHED**: „а Георгије 1066. године“ is the year this folder already holds off the title of doxologia's page, «Viața Cuviosului Gheorghe Ivirul (†1066)», whose body gave none. **AND THIS BOOK ADDS NO FOURTH DAY.** That Romanian page names three days for him — 24 May, when he fell asleep; 30 June, when the Georgians keep him with the Apostles; and 13 May, which it settles on — and this folder's Romanian row already carries all three in a note. **The Prologue keeps him on the 13 May the Romanian settled on**, which is corroboration of that choice from a fourth book and not a new day; nothing moved and no second-day note is owed. **New here**: that **he and Euthymius translated the Holy Scriptures into the Georgian tongue**. **`related_add: ["gabriel-the-iberian"]`**, the one of the four this folder did not carry; the reciprocal is in the same file. **`athanasius-the-athonite` was NOT added**: the lavra is John's part of the entry and not his, and a `related` row is owed for a person's own story. `types` untouched. **No `locations`**. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
